research.summary: Current endpoints are 16x16-bit planar tables (~32 MiB, 15 adds, 1024 B/candidate) vs 10x~26-bit tables (16 GiB, 9 adds, 640 B/candidate). Both stay on the doubling-free direct-add curve. Primary GitHub + arXiv evidence supports a third curve: tiny-table signed-digit/Lim-Lee combs that remove per-candidate DRAM reads in exchange for doublings+adds. Only abstract-level arXiv check was possible for one paper; no GPU timing is claimed.

findings.title: Signed-digit multi-comb with KB-scale table instead of GB-scale planar tables
findings.mechanism: Replace per-candidate random reads of 16x64KB or 10x~1.6GB planar windows with bitcoin-core style multi-comb: split 256-bit scalar into BLOCKS interleaved combs of TEETH bits with SPACING, precompute BLOCKS*(2^(TEETH-1)) points, then loop SPACING times doing BLOCKS adds + 1 doubling. Default (11,6) is 22 kB total.

sources.supports: Table size is BLOCKS*(2^(TEETH-1)) storages; adds=BLOCKS*SPACING, doublings=SPACING-1; default 11x6 = 22 kB

sources.locator: README Secp256k1 Point Multiplication + Bottlenecks/Global Memory Access
sources.supports: 16 chunks x 2 bytes = 1048576 points ~67MB needs 16*64 bytes DRAM per key; author states GTable random access without coalescing is probably main bottleneck and ~20x vs no precomputation

sources.locator: Abstract + Subjects (metadata only, full text not verified)
sources.supports: Paper compares M-ary method against fixed-base comb/sliding-window and reports author-measured secp256k1 results; only abstract checked so no transfer claim to grinding

findings.new_vs_memory: Memory records planar 16-bit and 10-window 26-bit tables and a 772 MiB regression warning, plus bitcoin-core ecmult_gen_impl.h as a lead. It does not record a concrete tiny-table signed multi-comb (11,6)-style transfer that eliminates the runtime base table and DRAM path.
findings.large_gain_case: Removed work: 640-1024 bytes of random table reads per candidate plus 16 GiB/32 MiB residency, tiling, sampling checks and reserve handling. Added work: O(BLOCKS*SPACING) point adds and SPACING-1 doublings from a KB table resident in cache/constants. Gain case is DRAM/latency-bound grinding where table reads stall the EC chain; no percentage claimed.
findings.risks: Adds doublings back where current chain is doubling-free; register/shared pressure from longer chain; cmov/negation and recoding cost per candidate; different scalar reuse vs bitcoin-core single-shot use.
findings.falsification: Mac-only: CPU-extract recoding for (11,6) and (43,6)-style configs, count adds/doubles vs 16x16-bit baseline and verify k*G against OpenSSL for random grind scalars; compile stub kernel for register/shared estimate only, no timing claim.

findings.title: Tunable Lim-Lee / M-ary (w,d) sweep between 512KB and 67MB
findings.mechanism: Use Lim-Lee comb parameter w (rows) and d=256/w (columns): table 2^w-1 points, evaluation (d-1) doublings + ~(d-1) adds. M-ary generalization in arXiv paper exposes radix/memory knob with stated Theta(Q log p / log Q) time vs Theta(Q log p / log^2 Q) memory. Sweep w=8 (255 pts ~16KB) to w=16 against current 16x16-bit to find cache-resident sweet spot instead of jumping to 16 GiB.

sources.supports: Author explicitly lists geometry trade: 8 chunks x 4 bytes needs 2TB, 32 chunks x 1 byte is 512KB but still not constants; 22/23-bit hybrid considered but lacked DRAM

sources.locator: Abstract time/memory complexity + fixed-base comb baseline table (metadata only)
sources.supports: Paper states M-ary vs fixed-base-comb/sliding-window comparison and complexity formulas; author-measured 59% encryption-time / 30% memory figures are ElGamal/NS3 workload, not grinding throughput
Shows comb geometry is explicitly parameterizable with efficiency guards, supporting a sweep rather than fixed endpoints

findings.new_vs_memory: Memory notes wide-table transfer and small/wide runtime comparison but not a systematic Lim-Lee (w,d) / M-ary radix sweep at KB-MB scale with doublings reintroduced; distinct from rejected epoch/window-family SHA scan and from deferred-Y/folding already inherited.
findings.large_gain_case: Removed work: 16 GiB table build/tiles/loads and large random DRAM fanout. Added work: small-table build once plus per-candidate doublings and adds. Large only if a cache-resident w fits occupancy/register budget while DRAM stalls dominate; no invented hit-rate or speedup.
findings.risks: Per-candidate doublings increase arithmetic and live state; optimal w is GPU-occupancy specific; paper gains do not transfer to per-candidate grind; builder/loader comparison must be bounded.
findings.falsification: Mac-only: enumerate w=4..16 table bytes and d-1 double/add counts, check cache-residency hypothesis against PR60 shared/register budget (128 regs prepare, 80 regs finish) without claiming GPU time.

research.next_question: What (BLOCKS,TEETH,SPACING) or (w,d) point keeps the table in cache/constants within PR60 register/shared budget while minimizing adds+doubles per grind candidate on CPU reference counts?
